report.incidentSummary: Starting at 10:33 IST (05:03 UTC) on 2026-10-22, incoming KYC status webhooks from external provider kyc-agency were rejected by kyc-service with HTTP 500 'signature verification failed'. Because status update webhooks were rejected, completed KYC applications could not transition out of 'pending', driving the pending application count from ~340 to over 2,000 and blocking new user onboarding. Internal services experienced no deployments or configuration updates in the preceding 7 days, whereas kyc-service intermittently accepted webhooks across all regions, pointing to an uncoordinated canary or phased signing key rotation by the external agency.
report.rootCauseStatement: External provider kyc-agency initiated an unannounced or canary rollout of an updated webhook signing key or signature payload format around 05:03 UTC, causing kyc-service to reject approximately 85% of incoming status webhooks with HTTP 500 ('signature verification failed') while a minority of webhooks from unmigrated agency nodes still verified successfully.

hypotheses.cause: External provider kyc-agency initiated a phased/canary rollout of a rotated webhook signing key or altered signature format without prior coordination, causing kyc-service to reject incoming webhooks from upgraded agency nodes with HTTP 500 'signature verification failed', while a minority of requests from unmigrated nodes still verify with HTTP 200.
hypotheses.rationale: kyc-service and message-queue had zero deployments or configuration updates in the preceding 7 days (ev_4, ev_7). At 05:03:02.500Z, kyc-service immediately began emitting HTTP 500 errors specifically citing 'signature verification failed' on POST /hooks/kyc from provider kyc-agency (ev_12, ev_13). Meanwhile, HTTP 200 successes continued intermittently across all regions (hyd-a, mum-a, mum-b) running the identical version 1.15.3 (ev_14), ruling out a single bad instance or region and mirroring historical incident PIR-2020 where signing key mismatch caused webhook rejections.

hypotheses.cause: Severely elevated processing and transmission latency at kyc-agency caused webhook delivery timestamps to exceed kyc-service's replay/timestamp tolerance window, leading to HMAC verification failures on delayed requests while timely requests continue to pass.
hypotheses.rationale: Outbound latency to kyc-agency spiked around 04:50 UTC (ev_1, ev_9), but signature failures began abruptly at 05:03:02Z rather than tracking latency ramps. Furthermore, successful status 200 webhooks continued to process across all regions without correlation to delivery latency windows (ev_14, ev_19), and kyc-service does not report clock skew warnings.

facts.statement: kyc-service outbound latency to kyc-agency (agency_latency_p95_ms) degraded from ~1,800 ms prior to 04:50 UTC to 4,875 ms at 05:00 UTC and remained between 5,500 ms and 6,200 ms through 08:00 UTC.
kyc_pending_count was stable between 336 and 341 until 04:55 UTC, then increased monotonically from 363 at 05:00 UTC to 2,024 by 07:55 UTC.
There were zero deployments, configuration changes, or feature flag updates for kyc-service or message-queue between 2026-10-15 and 2026-10-22 08:00 UTC.

At 2026-10-22T05:03:02.500Z, kyc-service began logging HTTP 500 errors on 'POST /hooks/kyc' from provider kyc-agency with error message 'signature verification failed', totaling 180 failures by 08:00 UTC.
During the same window from 05:03 UTC to 08:00 UTC, kyc-service successfully verified and processed 32 status webhooks with HTTP 200 across multiple regions (hyd-a, mum-a, mum-b) on version 1.15.3.
message-queue logged only standard INFO-level rebalance events throughout the window; consumer group kyc-hooks experienced only two standard rebalances with zero error logs.
Past incident PIR-2020 (2026-08-21) had identical symptoms where KYC webhooks were rejected due to an uncoordinated signing key rotation, resolved by supporting dual keys.

inferences.statement: Internal deployment regressions and internal configuration drifts are eliminated as causes because no changes occurred on kyc-service or message-queue in the preceding 7 days.
The issue is not localized to a single faulty host or region, because both HTTP 200 successes and HTTP 500 signature verification failures occurred concurrently across hyd-a, mum-a, and mum-b.

The rejection of incoming status webhooks at the HTTP verification layer directly caused the pending KYC count backlog, as valid verification decisions from kyc-agency were dropped before ingestion into message-queue.
The ~85% failure rate and ~15% success rate indicate that kyc-agency is mid-rollout of an infrastructure or key update, sending requests from both migrated and unmigrated nodes.

assumptions.statement: kyc-agency is conducting an unannounced rollout or key rotation where upgraded nodes sign with a new secret or header structure and unupgraded nodes use the legacy secret.
kyc-service evaluates incoming webhooks against a single static signing secret without fallback or multi-key validation.

timeline.event: kyc-service begins logging slow outbound submission responses from kyc-agency as p95 latency begins rising from ~1.8s.
Outbound latency to kyc-agency climbs to 4,875 ms; kyc_pending_count begins rising above baseline from 363.
First incoming webhook on POST /hooks/kyc is rejected by kyc-service with HTTP 500 'signature verification failed'.
A webhook event succeeds with HTTP 200 in hyd-a ('KYC KY-721042 status webhook processed: verified'), proving verification still works for legacy/subset requests.
Onboarding operations reports incident INC-9711 as pending KYC applications exceed 1,200.
Pending applications reach 2,024 as 180 total webhook verification failures have occurred against only 32 successes.

confidence.rationale: Internal changes are conclusively ruled out by complete absence of deployments, flag updates, and secret reloads over 7 days. The failure mode is uniquely identified in logs as signature verification failure at the HTTP perimeter starting precisely at 05:03:02 UTC. The remaining 0.15 uncertainty reflects lack of direct partner visibility into kyc-agency's internal deployment registry and raw request headers.

gaps.impact: Low; exact counts and onset timestamps for HTTP 500 signature verification failures and HTTP 200 successes were obtained directly from structured log aggregations.

gaps.description: Log records did not preserve raw incoming HTTP signature headers (e.g. X-Agency-Key-Id, X-Signature-Version).
gaps.impact: Moderate; prevented inspecting the specific header difference (key ID versus hashing algorithm versus timestamp) distinguishing the 180 failing requests from the 32 passing ones.

recommendedActions.action: Contact partner operations at kyc-agency immediately to confirm active webhook signing key rotation or canary deployment and obtain the new signing key.
recommendedActions.rationale: The incoming signature failures started at 05:03 UTC without any internal service modifications, indicating an upstream credential or signature change.
recommendedActions.verification: Agency confirms rollout of new signing key or payload format and provides the updated secret.

recommendedActions.action: Configure kyc-service to accept dual webhook signing secrets (the active key and the new agency key simultaneously), replicating the fix from PIR-2020.
recommendedActions.rationale: Supporting both keys ensures incoming webhooks from both legacy and migrated agency nodes verify cleanly during key transitions.
recommendedActions.verification: HTTP 500 logs on POST /hooks/kyc drop to zero and HTTP 200 log rate rises to match incoming agency webhook volume.

recommendedActions.action: Request kyc-agency to replay all webhook status notifications delivered between 05:03:02 UTC and the fix time, or trigger a status reconciliation query for all applications in pending state.
recommendedActions.rationale: The 180+ dropped webhooks left completed user verifications unapplied in our database, causing pending application count to remain inflated.
recommendedActions.verification: kyc_pending_count metric declines from ~2,024 back to normal operational baseline (~340).

recommendedActions.action: Update kyc-service webhook handler to log incoming signature key IDs and return HTTP 401 instead of HTTP 500 when signature validation fails.
recommendedActions.rationale: Returning 500 masks authentication/signature mismatches as internal server faults, and logging key identifiers accelerates diagnosis of future rotations.
recommendedActions.verification: Synthetic test webhook with invalid signature emits structured warning log containing key ID and responds with HTTP 401.
